claims.text: Atom probe tomography can elucidate elemental redistribution at nanoprecipitates during oxidation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA.
The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a dual-nanoprecipitation microstructure with finely distributed nanoprecipitates.
The proposed intervention is high-temperature oxidation in a controlled oxygen-rich environment.
The oxidation conditions are intended to be comparable to conditions encountered in gas turbines, power plants, or aerospace components.
The alloy's nanoprecipitates are enriched in Al and Ti.
Al- and Ti-enriched nanoprecipitates influence oxide-scale formation.
High-temperature exposure causes elemental redistribution from the nanoprecipitates, particularly redistribution of Al and Ti.
Redistribution of Al and Ti from nanoprecipitates promotes formation of a protective oxide scale.
APT can track compositional shifts and connect nanoprecipitate evolution with changes in oxidation behavior.
Oxidized specimens will exhibit significant Al or Ti segregation or enrichment at the oxide/metal interface relative to the as-fabricated state.
Cast and wrought counterparts have nanoprecipitate distributions different from those of the additively manufactured alloy.
Differences in nanoprecipitate distributions between processing routes correspond to differences in oxidation behavior.
APT resolution limitations and additive-manufacturing-induced artifacts may hinder dynamic capture of elemental redistribution during oxidation.
The experiment will compare oxidized specimens with as-fabricated unoxidized specimens and cast or wrought counterparts.
TEM and EDS will be used to validate microstructure and measure oxide-scale composition and thickness.
